blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Respecting work-life balance in the UK is not a trendy slogan — it is a professional habit that says something about you. Managers who regularly email their team at 10 p.m., even with good intentions, quietly make people feel they should be working too. British teams notice this fast, and morale drops.

A better habit is to write your late emails in the drafts folder and send them in the morning. You still get the thought out of your head; the team still gets protection. If something is truly urgent, call — that is a different signal. Otherwise, respect the boundary you would want for yourself.

The best British managers I know protect their team's evenings as if they were their own, and they are usually the ones whose teams stay longest, work hardest and respect them most.

items.q: According to the text, what happens when managers regularly email their team at 10 p.m.?
options: Nothing changes, as long as intentions are good
The manager is seen as more committed
People feel they should be working too, and morale drops
The team responds faster the next day
items.why: "quietly make people feel they should be working too… morale drops."

items.q: What is the "better habit" the author recommends for late emails?
options: Only email the team on weekdays
Send them immediately so they are not forgotten
Ask a colleague to send them the next day
Write them in the drafts folder and send them in the morning
items.why: "write your late emails in the drafts folder and send them in the morning."

items.q: The author says that calling is "a different signal". This suggests that…
options: phone calls are always more polite than emails
managers should never contact the team after hours
a call after hours should be reserved for something truly urgent
the team prefers calls to emails in general
items.why: Inferência: "If something is truly urgent, call" — a ligação marca urgência real, não é o canal cotidiano.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Protecting the team's evenings can strengthen loyalty.
Boundaries you want for yourself should apply to others too.
Sending late emails at once proves a manager is more dedicated.
Good intentions do not remove the pressure a late email creates.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta o oposto — mandar tarde, mesmo bem-intencionado, derruba a moral; não prova dedicação.

items.q: What does the final paragraph suggest about managers who protect their team's evenings?
options: They are less productive than other managers
They avoid difficult conversations
They tend to keep and earn the respect of their teams
They rarely reach senior positions
items.why: Inferência: "whose teams stay longest, work hardest and respect them most" — proteger o limite fortalece a equipe.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily orientando o novo gestor. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, before your team even starts next week, let's agree one simple rule about after-hours emails. It will save you a lot of trouble later.

Here in the UK, people watch what a manager does far more than what a manager says. If you email at ten in the evening, even to be helpful, half the team will quietly assume they ought to reply. Nobody complains — they just feel it, and over a few weeks the mood in the room changes.

My advice is simple. When a thought comes to you late, write the email, but leave it in your drafts. Get it out of your head so you can sleep, then send it in the morning. The team gets a clear boundary, and you lose nothing.

The one exception is a real emergency. If it genuinely cannot wait, don't email — pick up the phone. A call at that hour tells people it is serious, and they respect that.

Do this well, and you'll find the same thing I've seen again and again: the managers who guard their team's evenings are the ones whose people stay the longest and work the hardest for them.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily want the new manager to agree on before the team starts?
options: A target for email response times
A simple rule about after-hours emails
A rule about weekly meetings
A dress code for the office
items.why: "let's agree one simple rule about after-hours emails."

items.q: According to Emily, why does emailing at ten in the evening cause a problem in the UK?
options: It breaks a formal company policy
The manager looks disorganised
The emails are often ignored overnight
Half the team will quietly assume they ought to reply
items.why: "half the team will quietly assume they ought to reply… the mood in the room changes."

items.q: What is Emily's advice when a work thought comes late at night?
options: Send the email at once so it is not forgotten
Wait until the next meeting to raise it
Write it, leave it in drafts, and send it in the morning
Message a colleague to handle it
items.why: "write the email, but leave it in your drafts… then send it in the morning."

items.q: Why does Emily say a phone call is different from an email in an emergency?
options: Calls are cheaper than emails after hours
A call is quicker to make than an email
The team dislikes reading emails at night
A call signals that the matter is genuinely serious
items.why: Inferência: "A call at that hour tells people it is serious" — a ligação é reservada ao que realmente não pode esperar.

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's overall message to the manager?
options: Rules about emails rarely make any real difference
Managers should never contact their team outside work hours
Protecting the team's evenings pays off in loyalty and effort
British teams are too sensitive about emails
items.why: Inferência: ela liga o hábito de proteger as noites da equipe a pessoas que "stay the longest and work the hardest".

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Respecting work-life balance is not a trendy slogan." Something trendy is…
options: fashionable or currently popular
difficult to understand
required by law
old-fashioned and rarely used
items.why: Trendy = da moda, o que está em alta no momento.

items.q: "After a month of late emails, team morale dropped noticeably." Morale is…
options: the company's ethical code
the size of the team
the number of hours worked
the general mood and confidence of the team
items.why: Morale = moral, o ânimo e a confiança do grupo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Sending work messages at midnight crosses a ___ that most people expect to be protected."
options: protection
habit
boundary
slogan
items.why: Boundary = limite; é o limite entre vida e trabalho que se atravessa.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Keep the note in your ___ overnight and send it once the office opens."
options: morale
boundary
drafts folder
slogan
items.why: Drafts folder = pasta de rascunhos, onde o e-mail espera até de manhã.

items.q: "Writing late but sending in the morning gives the team real protection." Protection here means…
options: a legal guarantee in the contract
a backup copy of the message
extra pay for late work
a shield that keeps their evenings free from work pressure
items.why: Protection = proteção; aqui, preservar as noites da equipe da pressão do trabalho.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em conversas sobre equipe e limites. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's set expectations with the team before they start." To set expectations means to…
options: review last year's results
make clear in advance what is and isn't expected
lower the team's targets
raise the team's workload
items.why: Set expectations = deixar claro de antemão o que se espera (e o que não).

items.q: "A manager who emails at 10 p.m. sends the wrong signal." To send a signal means to…
options: give a formal order
make a phone call
block a message
communicate a message indirectly through behaviour
items.why: Send a signal = passar uma mensagem implícita pelo comportamento — ligar, por exemplo, sinaliza urgência real.

items.q: "They agreed the rule but never followed through on it." They…
options: passed it to another team
changed it completely
explained it badly
failed to carry it out in practice
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Good managers look out for their team's evenings." To look out for someone means to…
options: wait for them to arrive
protect and care for their interests
search for a replacement
watch them closely for mistakes
items.why: Look out for = zelar por, cuidar dos interesses de alguém.

items.q: "When a call genuinely can't wait, don't put it off — pick up the phone." To put something off means to…
options: hand it to someone else
cancel it entirely
write it down
delay it to a later time
items.why: Put off = adiar; se é urgente de verdade, não se adia.
